Erlang/OTP SSH is the built-in SSH server component of the Erlang/OTP platform.

A critical vulnerability was discovered in the Erlang/OTP SSH server, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands remotely without authentication by crafting specific SSH protocol messages. In `/app/workspace/otp_src_27.3.2` we provide the source code of an affected version of Erlang/OTP SSH server.

Try to investigate which type of ssh message will cause this attack, and fix this bug. After the bugfix, the server should maintain normal SSH behavior and block this type of attack. The unauthorized ssh message should not be able to execute any system commands.

Just do the fix inside the provided code. No need to build and start the Erlang/OTP server.

Now let me look at the key SSH message handling and connection files. Based on the vulnerability description (unauthenticated command execution via SSH protocol messages), I should focus on:

1. Message handling (`ssh_message.erl`, `ssh_connection.erl`)
2. Authentication (`ssh_auth.erl`, `ssh_fsm_userauth_server.erl`)
3. Connection handler (`ssh_connection_handler.erl`)
4. CLI/exec functionality (`ssh_cli.erl`)

   375→decode(<<?BYTE(?SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_REQUEST), ?UINT32(Recipient),
   376→	 ?DEC_BIN(RequestType,__0), ?BYTE(Bool), Data/binary>>=Bytes) ->
   377→    try
   378→        #ssh_msg_channel_request{
   379→           recipient_channel = Recipient,
   380→           request_type = ?unicode_list(RequestType),
   381→           want_reply = erl_boolean(Bool),
   382→           data  = Data

   385→            %% Faulty, RFC4254 says:
   386→            %% "If the request is not recognized or is not
   387→            %% supported for the channel, SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_FAILURE is returned."
   388→            %% So we provoke such a message to be sent
   389→            #ssh_msg_channel_request{
   390→               recipient_channel = Recipient,
   391→               request_type = faulty_msg,
   392→               data = Bytes
   393→              }
   394→    end;

   572→%%%
   573→%%% Encode/decode ssh public/private keys
   574→%%%
   575→
   576→%%%-------- public key --------
   577→ssh2_pubkey_encode(#'RSAPublicKey'{modulus = N, publicExponent = E}) ->
   578→    <<?STRING(<<"ssh-rsa">>), ?Empint(E), ?Empint(N)>>;
   579→
   580→ssh2_pubkey_encode({Y,  #'Dss-Parms'{p = P, q = Q, g = G}}) ->
   581→    <<?STRING(<<"ssh-dss">>), ?Empint(P), ?Empint(Q), ?Empint(G), ?Empint(Y)>>;
   582→
   583→ssh2_pubkey_encode({#'ECPoint'{point = Q}, {namedCurve,OID}}) when OID == ?'id-Ed25519' orelse
   584→                                                                   OID == ?'id-Ed448' ->
   585→    {KeyType, _} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   586→    <<?STRING(KeyType), ?Estring(Q)>>;
   587→
   588→ssh2_pubkey_encode(#'ECPrivateKey'{parameters = {namedCurve,OID},
   589→                                   publicKey = Key}) when OID == ?'id-Ed25519' orelse
   590→                                                          OID == ?'id-Ed448' ->
   591→    {KeyType, _} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   592→    <<?STRING(KeyType), ?Estring(Key)>>;
   593→
   594→ssh2_pubkey_encode(#'ECPrivateKey'{parameters = {namedCurve,OID},
   595→                                   publicKey = Key}) ->
   596→    {KeyType,Curve} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   597→    <<?STRING(KeyType), ?STRING(Curve), ?Estring(Key)>>;
   598→
   599→ssh2_pubkey_encode({#'ECPoint'{point = Q}, {namedCurve,OID}}) ->
   600→    {KeyType,Curve} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   601→    <<?STRING(KeyType), ?STRING(Curve), ?Estring(Q)>>.
   602→
   603→%%%--------
   604→ssh2_pubkey_decode(KeyBlob) ->
   605→    {Key,_RestBlob} = ssh2_pubkey_decode2(KeyBlob),
   606→    Key.
   607→    
   608→ssh2_pubkey_decode2(<<?UINT32(7), "ssh-rsa",
   609→                      ?DEC_INT(E, _EL),
   610→                      ?DEC_INT(N, _NL),
   611→                      Rest/binary>>) ->
   612→    {#'RSAPublicKey'{modulus = N,
   613→                     publicExponent = E
   614→                    }, Rest};
   615→ssh2_pubkey_decode2(<<?UINT32(7), "ssh-dss",
   616→                      ?DEC_INT(P, _PL),
   617→                      ?DEC_INT(Q, _QL),
   618→                      ?DEC_INT(G, _GL),
   619→                      ?DEC_INT(Y, _YL),
   620→                      Rest/binary>>) ->
   621→    {{Y, #'Dss-Parms'{p = P,
   622→                      q = Q,
   623→                      g = G}
   624→     }, Rest};
   625→
   626→ssh2_pubkey_decode2(<<?DEC_BIN(SshCurveName,SCNL), Rest0/binary>>) ->
   627→    {Pub, Rest} =
   628→        case {SshCurveName, Rest0} of
   629→            {<<"ecdsa-sha2-", _/binary>>,
   630→             <<?DEC_BIN(_Curve, _IL),
   631→               ?DEC_BIN(Q, _QL),
   632→               Rest1/binary>>} ->  {Q, Rest1};
   633→            
   634→            {<<"ssh-ed",_/binary>>,
   635→             <<?DEC_BIN(Key, _L),
   636→               Rest1/binary>>} ->  {Key, Rest1}
   637→        end,
   638→    OID = ssh_curvename2oid(SshCurveName),
   639→    {{#'ECPoint'{point = Pub}, {namedCurve,OID}},
   640→     Rest}.
   641→
   642→%%%-------- private key --------
   643→
   644→%% dialyser... ssh2_privkey_decode(KeyBlob) ->
   645→%% dialyser...     {Key,_RestBlob} = ssh2_privkey_decode2(KeyBlob),
   646→%% dialyser...     Key.
   647→%% See sshkey_private_serialize_opt in sshkey.c
   648→
   649→ssh2_privkey_encode(#'RSAPrivateKey'
   650→                    {version = 'two-prime', % Found this in public_key:generate_key/1 ..
   651→                     modulus = N,
   652→                     publicExponent = E,
   653→                     privateExponent = D,
   654→                     prime1 = P,
   655→                     prime2 = Q,
   656→                     %% exponent1, % D_mod_P_1
   657→                     %% exponent2, % D_mod_Q_1
   658→                     coefficient = IQMP
   659→                    }) ->
   660→    <<?STRING(<<"ssh-rsa">>),
   661→      ?Empint(N), % Yes, N and E is reversed relative pubkey format
   662→      ?Empint(E), % --"--
   663→      ?Empint(D),
   664→      ?Empint(IQMP),
   665→      ?Empint(P),
   666→      ?Empint(Q)>>;
   667→
   668→ssh2_privkey_encode(#'DSAPrivateKey'
   669→                    {version = 0,
   670→                     p = P,
   671→                     q = Q,
   672→                     g = G,
   673→                     y = Y,
   674→                     x = X
   675→                    }) ->
   676→    <<?STRING(<<"ssh-dss">>),
   677→      ?Empint(P),
   678→      ?Empint(Q),
   679→      ?Empint(G),
   680→      ?Empint(Y), % Publ key
   681→      ?Empint(X)  % Priv key
   682→    >>;
   683→
   684→ssh2_privkey_encode(#'ECPrivateKey'
   685→                    {version = 1,
   686→                     parameters = {namedCurve,OID},
   687→                     privateKey = Priv,
   688→                     publicKey = Pub
   689→                    }) when OID == ?'id-Ed25519' orelse
   690→                            OID == ?'id-Ed448' ->
   691→    {CurveName,_} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   692→    <<?STRING(CurveName),
   693→      ?STRING(Pub),
   694→      ?STRING(Priv)>>;
   695→
   696→ssh2_privkey_encode(#'ECPrivateKey'
   697→                    {version = 1,
   698→                     parameters = {namedCurve,OID},
   699→                     privateKey = Priv,
   700→                     publicKey = Q
   701→                    }) ->
   702→    {CurveName,_} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   703→    <<?STRING(CurveName),
   704→      ?STRING(CurveName), % SIC!
   705→      ?STRING(Q),
   706→      ?STRING(Priv)>>.
   707→      
   708→%%%--------
   709→ssh2_privkey_decode2(<<?UINT32(7), "ssh-rsa",
   710→                       ?DEC_INT(N, _NL), % Yes, N and E is reversed relative pubkey format
   711→                       ?DEC_INT(E, _EL), % --"--
   712→                       ?DEC_INT(D, _DL),
   713→                       ?DEC_INT(IQMP, _IQMPL),
   714→                       ?DEC_INT(P, _PL),
   715→                       ?DEC_INT(Q, _QL),
   716→                       Rest/binary>>) ->
   717→    {#'RSAPrivateKey'{version = 'two-prime', % Found this in public_key:generate_key/1 ..
   718→                      modulus = N,
   719→                      publicExponent = E,
   720→                      privateExponent = D,
   721→                      prime1 = P,
   722→                      prime2 = Q,
   723→                      %exponent1, % D_mod_P_1
   724→                      %exponent2, % D_mod_Q_1
   725→                      coefficient = IQMP
   726→                     }, Rest};
   727→ssh2_privkey_decode2(<<?UINT32(7), "ssh-dss",
   728→                       ?DEC_INT(P, _PL),
   729→                       ?DEC_INT(Q, _QL),
   730→                       ?DEC_INT(G, _GL),
   731→                       ?DEC_INT(Y, _YL), % Publ key
   732→                       ?DEC_INT(X, _XL), % Priv key
   733→                       Rest/binary>>) ->
   734→    {#'DSAPrivateKey'{version = 0,
   735→                      p = P,
   736→                      q = Q,
   737→                      g = G,
   738→                      y = Y,
   739→                      x = X
   740→                     }, Rest};
   741→
   742→ssh2_privkey_decode2(<<?DEC_BIN(SshCurveName,SCNL), Rest0/binary>>) ->
   743→    {Pub, Priv, Rest} =
   744→        case {SshCurveName, Rest0} of
   745→            {<<"ecdsa-sha2-",_/binary>>,
   746→             <<?DEC_BIN(_Curve, _IL),
   747→               ?DEC_BIN(Pub1, _QL),
   748→               ?DEC_BIN(Priv1, _PrivL),
   749→               Rest1/binary>>} ->
   750→                {Pub1, Priv1, Rest1};
   751→
   752→            {<<"ssh-ed",_/binary>>,
   753→             <<?DEC_BIN(Pub1, PL),
   754→               ?DEC_BIN(PrivPub, PPL),
   755→               Rest1/binary>>} ->
   756→               PL = PPL div 2,
   757→                <<Priv1:PL/binary, _/binary>> = PrivPub,
   758→                {Pub1, Priv1, Rest1}
   759→        end,
   760→    OID = ssh_curvename2oid(SshCurveName),
   761→    {#'ECPrivateKey'{version = 1,
   762→                     parameters = {namedCurve,OID},
   763→                     privateKey = Priv,
   764→                     publicKey = Pub
   765→                    }, Rest}.
   766→
   767→
   768→%% Description: Converts from the ssh name of elliptic curves to
   769→%% the OIDs.
   770→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   771→ssh_curvename2oid(<<"ssh-ed25519">>) -> ?'id-Ed25519';
   772→ssh_curvename2oid(<<"ssh-ed448">>  ) -> ?'id-Ed448';
   773→ssh_curvename2oid(<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp256">>) -> ?'secp256r1';
   774→ssh_curvename2oid(<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp384">>) -> ?'secp384r1';
   775→ssh_curvename2oid(<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp521">>) -> ?'secp521r1'.
   776→
   777→%% Description: Converts from elliptic curve OIDs to the ssh name.
   778→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   779→oid2ssh_curvename(?'id-Ed25519')-> {<<"ssh-ed25519">>, 'n/a'};
   780→oid2ssh_curvename(?'id-Ed448')  -> {<<"ssh-ed448">>,   'n/a'};
   781→oid2ssh_curvename(?'secp256r1') -> {<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp256">>, <<"nistp256">>};
   782→oid2ssh_curvename(?'secp384r1') -> {<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp384">>, <<"nistp384">>};
   783→oid2ssh_curvename(?'secp521r1') -> {<<"ecdsa-sha2-nistp521">>, <<"nistp521">>}.
   784→
   785→%%%================================================================
   786→%%%
   787→%%% Helper functions
   788→%%%
   789→
   790→bin_foldr(Fun, Acc, Bin) ->
   791→    lists:reverse(bin_foldl(Fun, Acc, Bin)).
   792→
   793→bin_foldl(_, Acc, <<>>) -> Acc;
   794→bin_foldl(Fun, Acc0, Bin0) ->
   795→    case Fun(Bin0,Acc0) of
   796→        {Bin0,Acc0} ->
   797→            Acc0;
   798→        {Bin,Acc} ->
   799→            bin_foldl(Fun, Acc, Bin)
   800→    end.
   801→
   802→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   803→decode_keyboard_interactive_prompts(<<>>, Acc) ->
   804→    lists:reverse(Acc);
   805→decode_keyboard_interactive_prompts(<<0>>, Acc) ->
   806→    lists:reverse(Acc);
   807→decode_keyboard_interactive_prompts(<<?DEC_BIN(Prompt,__0), ?BYTE(Bool), Bin/binary>>,
   808→				    Acc) ->
   809→    decode_keyboard_interactive_prompts(Bin, [{Prompt, erl_boolean(Bool)} | Acc]).
   810→
   811→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   812→erl_boolean(0) ->
   813→    false;
   814→erl_boolean(1) ->
   815→    true.
   816→
   817→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   818→decode_kex_init(<<?BYTE(Bool), ?UINT32(X)>>, Acc, 0) ->
   819→    list_to_tuple(lists:reverse([X, erl_boolean(Bool) | Acc]));
   820→decode_kex_init(<<?BYTE(Bool)>>, Acc, 0) ->
   821→    %% The mandatory trailing UINT32 is missing. Assume the value it anyhow must have
   822→    %% See rfc 4253 7.1
   823→    X = 0,
   824→    list_to_tuple(lists:reverse([X, erl_boolean(Bool) | Acc]));
   825→decode_kex_init(<<?DEC_BIN(Data,__0), Rest/binary>>, Acc, N) ->
   826→    BinParts = binary:split(Data, <<$,>>, [global]),
   827→    Process =
   828→        fun(<<>>, PAcc) ->
   829→                PAcc;
   830→           (Part, PAcc) ->
   831→                case byte_size(Part) > ?ALG_NAME_LIMIT of
   832→                    true ->
   833→                        ?LOG_DEBUG("Ignoring too long name", []),
   834→                        PAcc;
   835→                    false ->
   836→                        Name = binary:bin_to_list(Part),
   837→                        [Name | PAcc]
   838→                end
   839→        end,
   840→    Names = lists:foldr(Process, [], BinParts),
   841→    decode_kex_init(Rest, [Names | Acc], N - 1).
   842→

   844→%%%================================================================
   845→%%%
   846→%%% Signature decode/encode
   847→%%%
   848→
   849→decode_signature(<<?DEC_BIN(Alg,__0), ?UINT32(_), Signature/binary>>) ->
   850→    {binary_to_list(Alg), Signature}.
   851→
   852→
   853→encode_signature(#'RSAPublicKey'{}, SigAlg, Signature) ->
   854→    SignName = list_to_binary(atom_to_list(SigAlg)),
   855→    <<?Ebinary(SignName), ?Ebinary(Signature)>>;
   856→encode_signature({_, #'Dss-Parms'{}}, _SigAlg, Signature) ->
   857→    <<?Ebinary(<<"ssh-dss">>), ?Ebinary(Signature)>>;
   858→encode_signature({#'ECPoint'{}, {namedCurve,OID}}, _SigAlg, Signature) ->
   859→    {SshCurveName,_} = oid2ssh_curvename(OID),
   860→    <<?Ebinary(<<SshCurveName/binary>>), ?Ebinary(Signature)>>.

   867→
   868→ssh_dbg_trace_points() -> [ssh_messages, raw_messages].
   869→
   870→ssh_dbg_flags(ssh_messages) -> [c];
   871→ssh_dbg_flags(raw_messages) -> [c].
   872→
   873→ssh_dbg_on(P) when P==ssh_messages ;
   874→                   P==raw_messages ->
   875→    dbg:tp(?MODULE,encode,1,x),
   876→    dbg:tp(?MODULE,decode,1,x).
   877→
   878→ssh_dbg_off(P) when P==ssh_messages ;
   879→                    P==raw_messages ->
   880→    dbg:ctpg(?MODULE,encode,1),
   881→    dbg:ctpg(?MODULE,decode,1).
   882→
   883→ssh_dbg_format(ssh_messages, {call,{?MODULE,encode,[Msg]}}) ->
   884→    Name = string:to_upper(atom_to_list(element(1,Msg))),
   885→    ["Going to send ",Name,":\n",
   886→     wr_record(ssh_dbg:shrink_bin(Msg))
   887→    ];
   888→ssh_dbg_format(ssh_messages, {return_from, {?MODULE,encode,1}, _Ret}) ->
   889→    skip;
   890→
   891→ssh_dbg_format(ssh_messages, {call, {?MODULE,decode,[_]}}) ->
   892→    skip;
   893→ssh_dbg_format(ssh_messages, {return_from,{?MODULE,decode,1},Msg}) ->
   894→    Name = string:to_upper(atom_to_list(element(1,Msg))),
   895→    ["Received ",Name,":\n",
   896→     wr_record(ssh_dbg:shrink_bin(Msg)),
   897→     case Msg of
   898→         #ssh_msg_userauth_request{service = "ssh-connection",
   899→                                   method = "publickey",
   900→                                   data = <<_,?DEC_BIN(Alg,__0),_/binary>>} ->
   901→             io_lib:format("  data decoded: ~s ... ~n", [Alg]);
   902→
   903→         #ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "env",
   904→                                  data = <<?DEC_BIN(Var,__0),?DEC_BIN(Val,__1)>>} ->
   905→             io_lib:format("  data decoded: ~s = ~s~n", [Var, Val]);
   906→
   907→         #ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "exec",
   908→                                  data = <<?DEC_BIN(Cmnd,__0)>>} ->
   909→             io_lib:format("  data decoded: ~s~n", [Cmnd]);
   910→
   911→         #ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "pty-req",
   912→                                  data = <<?DEC_BIN(BTermName,_TermLen),
   913→                                           ?UINT32(Width),?UINT32(Height),
   914→                                           ?UINT32(PixWidth), ?UINT32(PixHeight),
   915→                                           Modes/binary>>} ->
   916→             io_lib:format("  data decoded: terminal = ~s~n"
   917→                           "                width x height = ~p x ~p~n"
   918→                           "                pix-width x pix-height = ~p x ~p~n"
   919→                           "                pty-opts = ~p~n",
   920→                           [BTermName, Width,Height, PixWidth, PixHeight,
   921→                            ssh_connection:decode_pty_opts(Modes)]);
   922→         _ ->
   923→             ""
   924→     end
   925→    ];
   926→
   927→ssh_dbg_format(raw_messages, {call,{?MODULE,decode,[BytesPT]}}) ->
   928→    ["Received plain text bytes (shown after decryption):\n",
   929→     io_lib:format("~p",[BytesPT])
   930→    ];
   931→ssh_dbg_format(raw_messages, {return_from, {?MODULE,decode,1}, _Ret}) ->
   932→    skip;
   933→
   934→ssh_dbg_format(raw_messages, {call, {?MODULE,encode,[_]}}) ->
   935→    skip;
   936→ssh_dbg_format(raw_messages, {return_from,{?MODULE,encode,1},BytesPT}) ->
   937→    ["Going to send plain text bytes (shown before encryption):\n",
   938→     io_lib:format("~p",[BytesPT])
   939→    ].

    26→
    27→-module(ssh_connection).
    28→-moduledoc """
    29→This module provides API functions to send SSH Connection Protocol events to the
    30→other side of an SSH channel.
    31→
    32→The [SSH Connection Protocol (RFC 4254)](http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4254.txt) is used by
    33→clients and servers, that is, SSH channels, to communicate over the SSH
    34→connection. The API functions in this module send SSH Connection Protocol
    35→events, which are received as messages by the remote channel handling the remote
    36→channel. The Erlang format of thoose messages is (see also
    37→[below](`t:event/0`)):
    38→
    39→`{ssh_cm,` `t:ssh:connection_ref/0` `,` `t:channel_msg/0` `}`
    40→
    41→If the `m:ssh_client_channel` behavior is used to implement the channel process,
    42→these messages are handled by
    43→[handle_ssh_msg/2](`c:ssh_client_channel:handle_ssh_msg/2`).
    44→""".
    45→-moduledoc(#{titles =>
    46→                 [{type,<<"General">>},
    47→                  {type,<<"Data Transfer">>},
    48→                  {type,<<"Closing a Channel">>},
    49→                  {type,<<"Pseudo-Terminal">>},
    50→                  {type,<<"Environment Variable">>},
    51→                  {type,<<"Shell or Command">>},
    52→                  {type,<<"Window Change">>},
    53→                  {type,<<"Signals">>},
    54→                  {type,<<"Exit Status">>}]}).
    55→
    56→-include("ssh.hrl").
    57→-include("ssh_connect.hrl").
    58→-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
    59→
    60→%% API
    61→-export([session_channel/2, session_channel/4,
    62→	 exec/4, shell/2, subsystem/4, send/3, send/4, send/5, 
    63→	 send_eof/2, adjust_window/3, setenv/5, close/2, reply_request/4,
    64→	 ptty_alloc/3, ptty_alloc/4]).
    65→
    66→%% Potential API currently unsupported and not tested
    67→-export([window_change/4, window_change/6,
    68→	 signal/3, exit_status/3]).
    69→
    70→%% Internal SSH application API
    71→-export([channel_data/5,
    72→         handle_msg/4,
    73→         handle_stop/1,
    74→
    75→         open_channel/4,
    76→
    77→	 channel_adjust_window_msg/2,
    78→	 channel_close_msg/1,
    79→	 channel_open_failure_msg/4,
    80→	 channel_open_msg/5,
    81→	 channel_status_msg/1,

    96→        ]).

   101→-type connection_ref() :: ssh:connection_ref().
   102→-type channel_id()     :: ssh:channel_id().
   103→
   104→-doc """
   105→The status of a request. Corresponds to the `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_SUCCESS` and
   106→`SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_FAILURE` values in
   107→[RFC 4254, Section 5.4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section-5.4).
   108→""".
   109→-type req_status() :: success | failure .
   110→-doc """
   111→The result of a call.
   112→
   113→If the request reached the peer, was handled and the response reached the
   114→requesting node the `t:req_status/0` is the status reported from the peer.
   115→
   116→If not, the `t:reason/0` indicates what went wrong:
   117→
   118→- **`closed`** - indicates that the channel or connection was closed when trying
   119→  to send the request
   120→
   121→- **`timeout`** - indicates that the operation exceeded a time limit
   122→""".
   123→-type reason() :: closed | timeout .
   124→
   125→-doc(#{}).
   126→-type result() :: req_status() | {error, reason()} .
   127→
   128→-doc """
   129→The valid values are `0` ("normal") and `1` ("stderr"), see
   130→[RFC 4254, Section 5.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#page-8).
   131→""".
   132→-type ssh_data_type_code() :: non_neg_integer(). % Only 0 and 1 are used
   133→

   136→
   137→-export_type([event/0,
   138→              channel_msg/0,
   139→              want_reply/0,
   140→              data_ch_msg/0,
   141→              eof_ch_msg/0,
   142→              signal_ch_msg/0,
   143→              exit_signal_ch_msg/0,
   144→              exit_status_ch_msg/0,

   147→              pty_ch_msg/0,

   149→              window_change_ch_msg/0,

   153→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   154→-type event() :: {ssh_cm, ssh:connection_ref(), channel_msg()}.
   155→-doc """
   156→As mentioned in the introduction, the
   157→[SSH Connection Protocol](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254) events are
   158→handled as messages. When writing a channel handling process without using the
   159→support by the `m:ssh_client_channel` behavior the process must handle thoose
   160→messages.
   161→""".
   162→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   163→-type channel_msg() ::  data_ch_msg()
   164→                      | eof_ch_msg()
   165→                      | closed_ch_msg()
   166→                      | pty_ch_msg()
   167→                      | env_ch_msg()
   168→                      | shell_ch_msg()
   169→                      | exec_ch_msg()
   170→                      | signal_ch_msg()
   171→                      | window_change_ch_msg()
   172→                      | exit_status_ch_msg()
   173→                      | exit_signal_ch_msg()
   174→                        .
   175→
   176→-doc """
   177→Messages that include a `WantReply` expect the channel handling process to call
   178→[ssh_connection:reply_request/4](`reply_request/4`) with the boolean value of
   179→`WantReply` as the second argument.
   180→""".
   181→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   182→-type want_reply() :: boolean().
   183→
   184→-doc """
   185→Data has arrived on the channel. This event is sent as a result of calling
   186→[ssh_connection:send/3,4,5](`send/3`).
   187→""".
   188→-doc(#{title => <<"Data Transfer">>,
   189→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.2"}).
   190→-type data_ch_msg() :: {data,
   191→                        ssh:channel_id(),
   192→                        ssh_data_type_code(),
   193→                        Data :: binary()
   194→                       } .
   195→-doc """
   196→Indicates that the other side sends no more data. This event is sent as a result
   197→of calling [ssh_connection:send_eof/2](`send_eof/2`).
   198→""".
   199→-doc(#{title => <<"Closing a Channel">>,
   200→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.3"}).
   201→-type eof_ch_msg() :: {eof,
   202→                       ssh:channel_id()
   203→                      } .
   204→-doc """
   205→A signal can be delivered to the remote process/service using the following
   206→message. Some systems do not support signals, in which case they are to ignore
   207→this message. There is currently no function to generate this event as the
   208→signals referred to are on OS-level and not something generated by an Erlang
   209→program.
   210→""".
   211→-doc(#{title => <<"Signals">>,
   212→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.9"}).
   213→-type signal_ch_msg() :: {signal,
   214→                          ssh:channel_id(),
   215→                          SignalName :: string()
   216→                         } .
   217→-doc """
   218→A remote execution can terminate violently because of a signal. Then this
   219→message can be received. For details on valid string values, see
   220→[RFC 4254](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section-6.10) Section 6.10, which
   221→shows a special case of these signals.
   222→""".
   223→-doc(#{title => <<"Exit Status">>,
   224→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.10"}).
   225→-type exit_signal_ch_msg() :: {exit_signal, ssh:channel_id(),
   226→                               ExitSignal :: string(),
   227→                               ErrorMsg :: string(),
   228→                               LanguageString :: string()} .
   229→-doc """
   230→When the command running at the other end terminates, the following message can
   231→be sent to return the exit status of the command. A zero `exit_status` usually
   232→means that the command terminated successfully. This event is sent as a result
   233→of calling [ssh_connection:exit_status/3](`exit_status/3`).
   234→""".
   235→-doc(#{title => <<"Exit Status">>,
   236→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.10"}).
   237→-type exit_status_ch_msg() :: {exit_status,
   238→                               ssh:channel_id(),
   239→                               ExitStatus :: non_neg_integer()
   240→                              } .
   241→-doc """
   242→This event is sent as a result of calling [ssh_connection:close/2](`close/2`).
   243→Both the handling of this event and sending it are taken care of by the
   244→`m:ssh_client_channel` behavior.
   245→""".
   246→-doc(#{title => <<"Closing a Channel">>,
   247→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.3"}).
   248→-type closed_ch_msg() :: {closed,
   249→                          ssh:channel_id()
   250→                         } .
   251→-doc """
   252→Environment variables can be passed to the shell/command to be started later.
   253→This event is sent as a result of calling [ssh_connection:setenv/5](`setenv/5`).
   254→""".

   347→-doc(#{equiv => session_channel/4}).

   359→is the id used as input to the other functions in this module.

   362→      ConnectionRef :: ssh:connection_ref(),

   364→      MaxPacketSize :: pos_integer() | undefined,
   365→      Timeout :: timeout(),
   366→      Result :: {ok, ssh:channel_id()} | {error, reason()} .

   368→session_channel(ConnectionRef, InitialWindowSize, MaxPacketSize, Timeout) ->

   379→    open_channel(ConnectionRef, Type, ChanData, undefined, undefined, Timeout).

   391→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   392→%% Description: Will request that the server start the
   393→%% execution of the given command. 
   394→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   395→-doc """
   396→Is to be called by a client-channel process to request that the server starts
   397→executing the given command. The result is several messages according to the
   398→following pattern. The last message is a channel close message, as the `exec`
   399→request is a one-time execution that closes the channel when it is done.
   400→
   401→- **N x [data message(s)](`t:data_ch_msg/0`)** - The result of executing the
   402→  command can be only one line or thousands of lines depending on the command.
   403→
   404→- **0 or 1 x [eof message](`t:eof_ch_msg/0`)** - Indicates that no more data is
   405→  to be sent.
   406→
   407→- **0 or 1 x [exit signal message](`t:exit_signal_ch_msg/0`)** - Not all systems
   408→  send signals. For details on valid string values, see RFC 4254, Section 6.10
   409→
   410→- **0 or 1 x [exit status message](`t:exit_status_ch_msg/0`)** - It is
   411→  recommended by the SSH Connection Protocol to send this message, but that is
   412→  not always the case.
   413→
   414→- **1 x [closed status message](`t:closed_ch_msg/0`)** - Indicates that the
   415→  `ssh_client_channel` started for the execution of the command has now been
   416→  shut down.
   417→
   418→See the User's Guide section on
   419→[One-Time Execution](using_ssh.md#one-time-execution) for examples.
   420→""".
   421→-spec exec(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, Command, Timeout) -> result() when
   422→      ConnectionRef :: ssh:connection_ref(),
   423→      ChannelId :: ssh:channel_id(),
   424→      Command :: string(),
   425→      Timeout :: timeout().
   426→
   427→exec(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, Command, TimeOut) ->
   428→    ssh_connection_handler:request(ConnectionRef, self(), ChannelId, "exec",
   429→				   true, [?string(Command)], TimeOut).

   431→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   432→%% Description: Will request that the user's default shell (typically
   433→%% defined in /etc/passwd in UNIX systems) be started at the other
   434→%% end.
   435→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   436→-doc """
   437→Is to be called by a client channel process to request that the user default
   438→shell (typically defined in /etc/passwd in Unix systems) is executed at the
   439→server end.
   440→
   441→Note: the return value is `ok` instead of `success` unlike in other functions in
   442→this module. This is a fault that was introduced so long ago that any change
   443→would break a large number of existing software.
   444→""".
   445→-spec shell(ConnectionRef, ChannelId) -> Result when
   446→      ConnectionRef :: ssh:connection_ref(),
   447→      ChannelId :: ssh:channel_id(),
   448→      Result :: ok | success | failure | {error, timeout} .
   449→
   450→shell(ConnectionRef, ChannelId) ->
   451→    ssh_connection_handler:request(ConnectionRef, self(), ChannelId,
   452→ 				   "shell", false, <<>>, 0).

   455→%% Description: Executes a predefined subsystem.

   458→Is to be called by a client-channel process for requesting to execute a
   459→predefined subsystem on the server.

   461→The function [`subsystem/4`](`subsystem/4`) and subsequent calls of
   462→[send/3,4,5](`send/3`) must be executed in the same process.

   485→-doc """

   487→
   488→Depending on input arguments equivalent to one of `send/5` calls specified below.
   489→
   490→Equivalent to [send(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, 0, Data, TimeOut)](`send/5`) if
   491→called with TimeOut being integer.
   492→
   493→Equivalent to [send(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, 0, Data, infinity)](`send/5`) if

   495→
   496→Equivalent to [send(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, Type, Data, infinity)](`send/5`) if

   631→%% Description: Sends a ssh connection protocol pty_req.

   633→-doc(#{equiv => ptty_alloc/4}).
   634→-doc(#{since => <<"OTP 17.5">>}).
   635→-spec ptty_alloc(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, Options) -> result() when
   636→      ConnectionRef :: ssh:connection_ref(),
   637→      ChannelId :: ssh:channel_id(),
   638→      Options  :: proplists:proplist().
   639→
   640→ptty_alloc(ConnectionRef, Channel, Options) ->

   643→
   644→-doc """
   645→Sends an SSH Connection Protocol `pty_req`, to allocate a pseudo-terminal. Is to
   646→be called by an SSH client process.
   647→
   648→Options:
   649→
   650→- **\{term, string()\}** - Defaults to _os:getenv("TERM")_ or _vt100_ if it is
   651→  undefined.
   652→
   653→- **\{width, integer()\}** - Defaults to 80 if `pixel_width` is not defined.
   654→
   655→- **\{height, integer()\}** - Defaults to 24 if `pixel_height` is not defined.
   656→
   657→- **\{pixel_width, integer()\}** - Is disregarded if `width` is defined.
   658→
   659→- **\{pixel_height, integer()\}** - Is disregarded if `height` is defined.
   660→
   661→- **\{pty_opts, \[\{posix_atom(), integer()\}]\}** - Option can be an empty
   662→  list. Otherwise, see possible _POSIX_ names in Section 8 in
   663→  [RFC 4254](http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4254.txt).
   664→""".
   665→-doc(#{since => <<"OTP 17.4">>}).
   666→-spec ptty_alloc(ConnectionRef, ChannelId, Options, Timeout) -> result() when
   667→      ConnectionRef :: ssh:connection_ref(),
   668→      ChannelId :: ssh:channel_id(),
   669→      Options  :: proplists:proplist(),
   670→      Timeout :: timeout().
   671→
   672→ptty_alloc(ConnectionRef, Channel, Options0, TimeOut) ->
   673→    TermData = backwards_compatible(Options0, []), % FIXME
   674→    {Width, PixWidth} = pty_default_dimensions(width, TermData),
   675→    {Height, PixHeight} = pty_default_dimensions(height, TermData),
   676→    pty_req(ConnectionRef, Channel,
   677→	    proplists:get_value(term, TermData, os:getenv("TERM", ?DEFAULT_TERMINAL)),
   678→	    proplists:get_value(width, TermData, Width),
   679→	    proplists:get_value(height, TermData, Height),
   680→	    proplists:get_value(pixel_widh, TermData, PixWidth),
   681→	    proplists:get_value(pixel_height, TermData, PixHeight),
   682→	    proplists:get_value(pty_opts, TermData, []), TimeOut
   683→	   ).

   723→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   724→%%% Send data on a channel/connection as result of for example
   725→%%% ssh_connection:send (executed in the ssh_connection_state machine)
   726→%%%
   727→
   728→-doc false.
   729→channel_data(ChannelId, DataType, Data0, 
   730→	     #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection,
   731→	     From) ->
   732→    case ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId) of
   733→	#channel{remote_id = Id, sent_close = false} = Channel0 ->
   734→            Data = ?to_binary(Data0),
   735→	    {SendList, Channel} =
   736→		update_send_window(Channel0#channel{flow_control = From}, DataType,
   737→				   Data, Connection),
   738→	    Replies = 
   739→		lists:map(fun({SendDataType, SendData}) -> 
   740→				  {connection_reply,
   741→				   channel_data_msg(Id,
   742→						    SendDataType,
   743→						    SendData)}
   744→			  end, SendList),
   745→	    FlowCtrlMsgs = flow_control(Replies, Channel, Cache),
   746→	    {Replies ++ FlowCtrlMsgs, Connection};
   747→	_ ->
   748→	    {[{channel_request_reply,From,{error,closed}}], Connection}
   749→    end.

   751→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   752→%%% Handle the channel messages on behalf of the ssh_connection_handler
   753→%%% state machine.
   754→%%%
   755→%%% Replies {Reply, UpdatedConnection}
   756→%%%
   757→
   758→-doc false.
   759→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_open_confirmation{recipient_channel = ChannelId, 
   760→					      sender_channel = RemoteId,
   761→					      initial_window_size = WindowSz,
   762→					      maximum_packet_size = PacketSz}, 
   763→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   764→    
   765→    #channel{remote_id = undefined} = Channel =
   766→	ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId), 
   767→    
   768→    ssh_client_channel:cache_update(Cache, Channel#channel{
   769→				     remote_id = RemoteId,
   770→				     recv_packet_size = max(32768, % rfc4254/5.2
   771→							    min(PacketSz, Channel#channel.recv_packet_size)
   772→							   ),
   773→				     send_window_size = WindowSz,
   774→				     send_packet_size = PacketSz}),
   775→    reply_msg(Channel, Connection0, {open, ChannelId});
   776→ 
   777→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_open_failure{recipient_channel = ChannelId,
   778→					 reason = Reason,
   779→					 description = Descr,
   780→					 lang = Lang},  
   781→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   782→    Channel = ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId), 
   783→    ssh_client_channel:cache_delete(Cache, ChannelId),
   784→    reply_msg(Channel, Connection0, {open_error, Reason, Descr, Lang});
   785→
   786→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_success{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   787→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, success);
   788→
   789→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_failure{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   790→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, failure);
   791→
   792→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_eof{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   793→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, {eof, ChannelId});
   794→   
   795→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_close{recipient_channel = ChannelId},   
   796→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   797→
   798→	case ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId) of
   799→		#channel{sent_close = Closed, remote_id = RemoteId,
   800→			 flow_control = FlowControl} = Channel ->

   802→		{CloseMsg, Connection} =

   815→			undefined -> [];
   816→			From ->

   818→		    end,

   902→    {ReplyMsg, NextChId} =
   903→        case ssh_connection_handler:retrieve(C, {tcpip_forward,ConnectedHost,ConnectedPort}) of
   904→            {ok, {ConnectToHost,ConnectToPort}} ->
   905→                case gen_tcp:connect(ConnectToHost, ConnectToPort, [{active,false}, binary]) of
   906→                    {ok,Sock} ->
   907→                        {ok,Pid} = ssh_connection_sup:start_channel(client, ConnectionSup, self(),
   908→                                                                   ssh_tcpip_forward_client, ChId,
   909→                                                                   [Sock], undefined, Options),

   912→                                                                 sys = "none",

  1271→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
  1272→%%% Returns pending responses to be delivered to the peer when a
  1273→%%% Channel/Connection closes
  1274→%%%
  1275→-doc false.
  1276→handle_stop(#connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0) ->
  1277→    {Connection, Replies} = 
  1278→	ssh_client_channel:cache_foldl(
  1279→          fun(Channel, {Connection1, Acc}) ->
  1280→                  {Reply, Connection2} =
  1281→                      reply_msg(Channel, Connection1,
  1282→                                {closed, Channel#channel.local_id}),
  1283→                  {Connection2, Reply ++ Acc}
  1284→          end, {Connection0, []}, Cache),
  1285→    ssh_client_channel:cache_delete(Cache),
  1286→    {Replies, Connection}.

  1437→start_cli(#connection{options = Options, 
  1438→		      cli_spec = CliSpec,
  1439→		      exec = Exec,
  1440→		      connection_supervisor = ConnectionSup}, ChannelId) ->
  1441→    case CliSpec of
  1442→        no_cli ->
  1443→            {error, cli_disabled};
  1444→        {CbModule, Args} ->
  1445→            ssh_connection_sup:start_channel(server, ConnectionSup, self(), CbModule, ChannelId, Args, Exec, Options)

  1449→start_subsystem(BinName, #connection{options = Options,
  1450→                                     connection_supervisor = ConnectionSup},
  1451→	       #channel{local_id = ChannelId}, _ReplyMsg) ->
  1452→    Name = binary_to_list(BinName),
  1453→    case check_subsystem(Name, Options) of
  1454→	{Callback, Opts} when is_atom(Callback), Callback =/= none ->
  1455→            ssh_connection_sup:start_channel(server, ConnectionSup, self(), Callback, ChannelId, Opts, undefined, Options);
  1456→        {none, _} ->
  1457→            {error, bad_subsystem};
  1458→	{_, _} ->
  1459→	    {error, legacy_option_not_supported}

  1486→
  1487→update_send_window(Channel, _, undefined,
  1488→		   #connection{channel_cache = Cache}) ->
  1489→    do_update_send_window(Channel, Cache);
  1490→
  1491→update_send_window(#channel{send_buf = SendBuffer} = Channel, DataType, Data,
  1492→		   #connection{channel_cache = Cache}) ->
  1493→    do_update_send_window(Channel#channel{send_buf = queue:in({DataType, Data}, SendBuffer)},
  1494→			  Cache).
  1495→
  1496→do_update_send_window(Channel0, Cache) ->
  1497→    {SendMsgs, Channel} = get_window(Channel0, []),
  1498→    ssh_client_channel:cache_update(Cache, Channel), 
  1499→    {SendMsgs, Channel}.
  1500→
  1501→get_window(#channel{send_window_size = 0
  1502→		   } = Channel, Acc) ->
  1503→    {lists:reverse(Acc), Channel};
  1504→get_window(#channel{send_packet_size = 0
  1505→		   } = Channel, Acc) ->
  1506→    {lists:reverse(Acc), Channel};
  1507→get_window(#channel{send_buf = Buffer, 
  1508→		    send_packet_size = PacketSize,
  1509→		    send_window_size = WindowSize0
  1510→		   } = Channel, Acc0) ->
  1511→    case queue:out(Buffer) of
  1512→	{{value, {_, Data} = Msg}, NewBuffer} ->
  1513→	    case handle_send_window(Msg, byte_size(Data), PacketSize, WindowSize0, Acc0) of
  1514→		{WindowSize, Acc, {_, <<>>}} ->
  1515→		    {lists:reverse(Acc), Channel#channel{send_window_size = WindowSize,
  1516→							 send_buf = NewBuffer}};
  1517→		{WindowSize, Acc, Rest} ->
  1518→		    get_window(Channel#channel{send_window_size = WindowSize,
  1519→					       send_buf = queue:in_r(Rest, NewBuffer)}, Acc)
  1520→	    end;
  1521→	{empty, NewBuffer} ->
  1522→	    {[], Channel#channel{send_buf = NewBuffer}}
  1523→    end.
  1524→
  1525→handle_send_window(Msg = {Type, Data}, Size, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) when Size =< WindowSize ->
  1526→    case Size =< PacketSize of
  1527→	true ->
  1528→	    {WindowSize - Size, [Msg | Acc], {Type, <<>>}};
  1529→	false ->
  1530→	    <<Msg1:PacketSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1531→	    {WindowSize - PacketSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}}
  1532→    end;
  1533→handle_send_window({Type, Data}, _, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) when WindowSize =< PacketSize ->
  1534→    <<Msg1:WindowSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1535→    {WindowSize - WindowSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}};
  1536→handle_send_window({Type, Data}, _, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) ->
  1537→    <<Msg1:PacketSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1538→    {WindowSize - PacketSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}}.

  1730→	     ?VEOL -> veol;
  1731→	     ?VEOL2 -> veol2;
  1732→	     ?VSTART -> vstart;
  1733→	     ?VSTOP -> vstop;
  1734→	     ?VSUSP -> vsusp;
  1735→	     ?VDSUSP -> vdsusp;
  1736→	     ?VREPRINT -> vreprint;
  1737→	     ?VWERASE -> vwerase;
  1738→	     ?VLNEXT -> vlnext;
  1739→	     ?VFLUSH -> vflush;
  1740→	     ?VSWTCH -> vswtch;
  1741→	     ?VSTATUS -> vstatus;
  1742→	     ?VDISCARD -> vdiscard;
  1743→	     ?IGNPAR -> ignpar;
  1744→	     ?PARMRK -> parmrk;
  1745→	     ?INPCK -> inpck;
  1746→	     ?ISTRIP -> istrip;
  1747→	     ?INLCR -> inlcr;
  1748→	     ?IGNCR -> igncr;
  1749→	     ?ICRNL -> icrnl;
  1750→	     ?IUCLC -> iuclc;
  1751→	     ?IXON -> ixon;
  1752→	     ?IXANY -> ixany;
  1753→	     ?IXOFF -> ixoff;
  1754→	     ?IMAXBEL -> imaxbel;
  1755→             ?IUTF8 -> iutf8; % RFC 8160
  1756→	     ?ISIG -> isig;
  1757→	     ?ICANON -> icanon;
  1758→	     ?XCASE -> xcase;
  1759→	     ?ECHO -> echo;
  1760→	     ?ECHOE -> echoe;
  1761→	     ?ECHOK -> echok;
  1762→	     ?ECHONL -> echonl;
  1763→	     ?NOFLSH -> noflsh;
  1764→	     ?TOSTOP -> tostop;
  1765→	     ?IEXTEN -> iexten;
  1766→	     ?ECHOCTL -> echoctl;
  1767→	     ?ECHOKE -> echoke;
  1768→	     ?PENDIN -> pendin;
  1769→	     ?OPOST -> opost;
  1770→	     ?OLCUC -> olcuc;
  1771→	     ?ONLCR -> onlcr;
  1772→	     ?OCRNL -> ocrnl;
  1773→	     ?ONOCR -> onocr;
  1774→	     ?ONLRET -> onlret;
  1775→	     ?CS7 -> cs7;
  1776→	     ?CS8 -> cs8;
  1777→	     ?PARENB -> parenb;
  1778→	     ?PARODD -> parodd;
  1779→	     ?TTY_OP_ISPEED -> tty_op_ispeed;
  1780→	     ?TTY_OP_OSPEED -> tty_op_ospeed;
  1781→	     _ -> Code
  1782→	 end,    
  1783→    [{Op, Value} | decode_pty_opts2(Tail)].
  1784→
  1785→
  1786→backwards_compatible([], Acc) ->
  1787→    Acc;
  1788→backwards_compatible([{hight, Value} | Rest], Acc) ->
  1789→    backwards_compatible(Rest, [{height, Value} | Acc]);
  1790→backwards_compatible([{pixel_hight, Value} | Rest], Acc) ->
  1791→    backwards_compatible(Rest, [{height, Value} | Acc]);
  1792→backwards_compatible([Value| Rest], Acc) ->
  1793→    backwards_compatible(Rest, [ Value | Acc]).
  1794→
  1795→
  1796→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
  1797→%%%
  1798→%%% Common part of handling channel messages meant for a cli (like "env", "exec" etc)
  1799→%%% Called at the finnish of handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request,...)
  1800→%%%
  1801→
  1802→handle_cli_msg(C0, ChId, Reply0) ->
  1803→    Cache = C0#connection.channel_cache,
  1804→    Ch0 = ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChId),
  1805→    case Ch0#channel.user of
  1806→        undefined ->
  1807→            case start_cli(C0, ChId) of
  1808→                {ok, Pid} ->
  1809→                    erlang:monitor(process, Pid),
  1810→                    Ch = Ch0#channel{user = Pid},
  1811→                    ssh_client_channel:cache_update(Cache, Ch),
  1812→                    reply_msg(Ch, C0, Reply0);
  1813→                {error, _Error} ->
  1814→                    Reply = {connection_reply, channel_failure_msg(Ch0#channel.remote_id)},
  1815→                    {[Reply], C0}
  1816→            end;
  1817→        
  1818→        _ ->
  1819→            reply_msg(Ch0, C0, Reply0)
  1820→    end.
  1821→
  1822→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
  1823→%%%
  1824→%%% TCP/IP forwarding
  1825→
  1826→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
  1827→%%%
  1828→%%% Request response handling on return to the calling ssh_connection_handler
  1829→%%% state machine.
  1830→%%% 
  1831→
  1832→channel_data_reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, DataType, Data) ->
  1833→    case ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Connection#connection.channel_cache, ChannelId) of
  1834→	#channel{recv_window_size = Size} = Channel ->
  1835→	    WantedSize = Size - byte_size(Data),
  1836→	    ssh_client_channel:cache_update(Connection#connection.channel_cache, 
  1837→                                     Channel#channel{recv_window_size = WantedSize}),
  1838→            reply_msg(Channel, Connection, {data, ChannelId, DataType, Data});
  1839→	undefined ->
  1840→	    {[], Connection}
  1841→    end.
  1842→
  1843→
  1844→reply_msg(ChId, C, Reply) when is_integer(ChId) ->
  1845→    reply_msg(ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(C#connection.channel_cache, ChId), C, Reply);
  1846→
  1847→reply_msg(Channel, Connection, {open, _} = Reply) ->
  1848→    request_reply_or_data(Channel, Connection, Reply);
  1849→reply_msg(Channel, Connection, {open_error, _, _, _} = Reply) ->
  1850→    request_reply_or_data(Channel, Connection, Reply);
  1851→reply_msg(Channel, Connection, success = Reply) ->
  1852→    request_reply_or_data(Channel, Connection, Reply);
  1853→reply_msg(Channel, Connection, failure = Reply) ->
  1854→    request_reply_or_data(Channel, Connection, Reply);
  1855→reply_msg(Channel, Connection, {closed, _} = Reply) ->
  1856→    request_reply_or_data(Channel, Connection, Reply);
  1857→reply_msg(undefined, Connection, _Reply) ->
  1858→    {[], Connection};
  1859→reply_msg(#channel{user = ChannelPid}, Connection, Reply) ->
  1860→    {[{channel_data, ChannelPid, Reply}], Connection}.
  1861→
  1862→
  1863→request_reply_or_data(#channel{local_id = ChannelId, user = ChannelPid}, 
  1864→		      #connection{requests = Requests} = 
  1865→		      Connection, Reply) -> 
  1866→    case lists:keysearch(ChannelId, 1, Requests) of
  1867→	{value, {ChannelId, From}} ->
  1868→	    {[{channel_request_reply, From, Reply}],
  1869→	     Connection#connection{requests = 
  1870→				       lists:keydelete(ChannelId, 1, Requests)}};
  1871→	false when (Reply == success) or (Reply == failure) ->
  1872→	    {[], Connection};
  1873→	false ->
  1874→	    {[{channel_data, ChannelPid, Reply}], Connection}
  1875→    end.
  1876→
  1877→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
  1878→-doc false.
  1879→send_environment_vars(ConnectionRef, Channel, VarNames) ->
  1880→    lists:foldl(
  1881→      fun(Var, success) ->
  1882→              case os:getenv(Var) of
  1883→                  false ->
  1884→                      success;
  1885→                  Value ->
  1886→                      setenv(ConnectionRef, Channel, false,
  1887→                             Var, Value, infinity)
  1888→              end
  1889→      end, success, VarNames).
